1) AR adjustment re-apply: create unapplied credit for 248,400 then apply credits to 4770/4771/4772 per Olivia's breakdown. This will create a short-lived unapplied credit (suspense) on our books but matches their remittance on their side; will require a JV to move VAT amounts between buckets.

2) Direct split using payment reallocation in ledger (preferred if ops allows): update AR allocation lines so payment is split across the three invoices without passing through suspense. Depends on whether settlement has cleared in the closed period.

Proposed accounting entries (draft):
- If using unapplied credit: DR Bank EUR 248,400  (already recorded at settlement)
  CR AR - invoice 4772 EUR 248,400 (reverse applied) -> then apply credits:
  CR AR - invoice 4770 EUR 78,400
  CR AR - invoice 4771 EUR 70,000
  CR AR - invoice 4772 EUR 100,000
- VAT reallocation JV (to move VAT between buckets)
  DR VAT Payable (standard 21%) EUR 36,150
  CR VAT Payable (zero-rate) EUR 0
  CR Revenue: reversal/adjustment entries per revmap codes (CS21 / DZ0)

I attached a quick workbook with the proposed GL allocations and revmap tags — Laura, can you confirm GL codes and whether we can run this without breaking the monthly close? If not, we'll use unapplied credit approach and mark as short-lived suspense.
